title: ESRGAN: Enhanced Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Networks
layout_note: Left half compares SRGAN's residual block with the BN-free version (a fat yellow arrow between them); right half shows the proposed RRDB as three dense blocks on a residual line, with the third dense block zoomed into a dashed-orange rounded panel at the far right.
grouping: Two halves headed by serif titles ('Residual Block (RB)', 'Residual in Residual Dense Block (RRDB)'); sub-labels 'SRGAN' and 'RB w/o BN' sit under the two left blocks. The zoomed dense block is enclosed by a dashed orange rounded rectangle, tied to its source block by two dashed orange lines.
shapes_depth: Layers are tall narrow flat rectangles with rotated labels, colour-coded by type: blue Conv, yellow BN, green ReLU/LReLU. Dense blocks are small orange rounded rectangles. Residual paths are thin blue lines bracketing each block, summing at small circled + glyphs; small green 'x beta' boxes mark residual scaling. Dense connections are coloured arcs (orange, green, blue) leaping over layers inside the zoom panel. No shadows, no 3-D.
proposed_highlight: The proposed RRDB takes the larger right half under its own heading, and its inner dense block is opened in a dashed orange zoom panel whose orange outline matches the dense-block fill; the removed BN layers are shown by their absence after a yellow arrow.
lesson: Show a design change as a before -> after pair joined by a fat arrow (deleted layers simply missing), then give the new block the larger half with its inner unit zoomed into a dashed panel tied back by guide lines.
notes: No venue printed on the arXiv first page; remembered as ECCV 2018 Workshops (PIRM), so venue = arXiv and year = arXiv preprint year. Chosen over Fig. 3 (the overall SRResNet-style generator, which the caption says is the borrowed basic architecture) because Fig. 4 draws the paper's own block. 'other' element = coloured dense-connection arcs.

arrangement.units: Left half: two residual blocks (before/after) side by side, unframed, joined by a yellow block arrow. Right half: RRDB on a residual line plus a dashed-orange rounded zoom panel of one dense block.
arrangement.inputs_as: a bare incoming line; no data shown
arrangement.shared: the three dense blocks are drawn as identical orange copies; only the last is zoomed

core.what: two titled halves side by side: on the left the SRGAN residual block turns into 'RB w/o BN' across a fat yellow arrow, on the wider right the proposed RRDB chains three orange Dense Blocks and opens the third in a dashed orange zoom panel

relations.form: before/after pair on the left: Conv-BN-ReLU-Conv-BN with a skip, then a fat yellow arrow, then Conv-ReLU-Conv with the yellow BN strips gone; RRDB follows to the right as the proposed block

RRDB is one horizontal blue line through three orange Dense Blocks, each followed by a small green beta scaling tag and a circled plus with its own skip, and an outer skip from the input to the final circled plus
a dashed orange line runs from the third Dense Block into a rounded dashed orange panel at the far right that draws its five Conv(+LReLU) layers on one line
inside the zoom every layer's output arcs over the line to every later layer, the dense connections drawn as nested coloured arcs
the three Dense Blocks are identical orange rounded boxes on one line, and the residual pattern (block, beta, add, skip) repeats at two nesting levels

channels.colour: layer type: blue = Conv, green = ReLU/LReLU, yellow = BN, orange = Dense Block; the dense-connection arcs are coloured by their source layer (orange, green, blue, ...), so orange and green also mean 'arc from layer k', and green also fills the beta scaling tags
channels.shape: tall bar = layer, rounded box = dense block, circled plus = addition, small tag = residual scaling beta
channels.line: solid blue lines = data and skips; coloured arcs = dense connections; dashed orange = the zoom callout
channels.frame: a dashed rounded orange panel = the inside of one dense block

quality.strengths: Removing BN is shown as the yellow strips vanishing across an arrow between two otherwise identical blocks, a pure geometric before/after; the contribution (RRDB) takes the wider half and its inner block is opened by an orange-tinted zoom that matches the block fill; the residual-in-residual nesting is legible as skips at two levels on one straight line.
quality.weaknesses: Arc colours re-use the layer-type palette, so orange and green carry two meanings inside the zoom; the beta scaling tags are tiny and unkeyed; the zoom panel's dense arcs pile up over the second and third layers, making individual connections hard to follow.

insights.structure: Two titled halves sit side by side: a before/after pair of residual blocks on the left and the proposed RRDB with a dashed zoom panel of its dense block on the right.
insights.data: No data is drawn; layers are tall coloured strips (blue Conv, yellow BN, green ReLU) and dense connections are coloured arcs hopping over the strips inside the zoom panel.
insights.emphasis: Removing BN is shown by the yellow BN strips vanishing after a fat yellow arrow, and RRDB is made the star by taking the wider half and opening its inner block in a dashed orange zoom.
insights.flow: Every block reads left to right along a thin blue main line, with residual bypass lines running above or below and rejoining at small circled + glyphs.
insights.avoid: The 'x beta' scaling boxes and their labels are tiny and the multicoloured dense arcs overlap, so the zoom panel is hard to read at print size.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
